_comment: What a blacksmith can forge. Engine data, not a campaign's: every realm's smithy works the same. 'cost' is paid out of the province's own stockpile (gold, grain, cattle, wood, stone, iron), 'batch' is how many the order delivers, and the four stats are 0..10 bars. Every number here is placeholder balance, meant to be tuned.

weapons.name: Bows
weapons.blurb: Cheap to make and quick to learn. Thins a charge long before it reaches the line.

weapons.name: Crossbows
weapons.blurb: Slow to wind, but a bolt goes through mail where an arrow turns. Anyone can be taught to aim one.

weapons.name: Swordsman
weapons.blurb: Well-balanced swords for disciplined infantry. Reliable in close combat and easy to arm in large numbers.

weapons.name: Pikeman
weapons.blurb: A hedge of points that horses will not ride into. Little use once a line is broken.

weapons.name: Cavalry
weapons.blurb: The costliest thing a province can raise, and the only one that decides a field in a single charge.

weapons.name: Maces
weapons.blurb: Crude, heavy, and indifferent to armour. What a smith forges when there is iron but no time.
